issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as type int, but the solution implementation declares the attribute as long (private long numberOfLoopings) and its getter returns long. This type mismatch between the specification and the provided solution may confuse students about which type to use for the attribute and its getter/constructor, and can lead to failing signature/attribute checks or inconsistent implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the attribute type with the UML. Change the RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings attribute in the solution to int (private int numberOfLoopings), ensure the constructor accepts an int and assigns it to this int field, and make the getter return int. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to specify long if that was intended. Ensure template, problem statement, and solution consistently use the same type.
